title: Semirandom coloring: where algorithms beat hardness
subtitle: A planted model with adversarial additions and explicitly conditional low-density hardness.

panels.title: Semirandom planted k-coloring
panels.note: Fixed k≥3, k divides n; balanced planted parts; adversary may add cross-part edges.
panels.xLabel: np / (k ln n) · fixed-k, ε→0 reference

verifiedRecords.quality: Certify an optimal k-coloring with high probability
verifiedRecords.graph: Balanced planted k-partition; each cross-part edge independently present with probabilityp; adversary only adds cross-part edges
verifiedRecords.output: Proper coloring, certified optimal in the high-density regime
verifiedRecords.probability: With high probability over initial random graph; uniform over permitted adversarial cross-part edge additions.
verifiedRecords.notes: For fixed k and large n the log term dominates. Marker1 is only a limiting normalized density. Exact k dependence is retained, and C₀ is not numerically instantiated.

verifiedRecords.quality: No polynomial-time k-coloring with high probability unless NP⊆RP
verifiedRecords.probability: Conditional computational hardness unless NP⊆RP; uniform over permitted adversarial cross-part edge additions.
verifiedRecords.notes: The fixed-k normalized boundary approaches(1−ε)/2. This is not an information-theoretic impossibility: a planted coloring exists.

relatedResults.quality: Always outputs a k-coloring on k-colorable graphs
relatedResults.graph: Same semirandom distribution controls expected computation
relatedResults.probability: Always correct on k-colorable inputs; expected polynomial work in stated regime
relatedResults.notes: Unknown absolute constant C₀ is not assigned a numeric marker.
relatedResults.computation: Expected polynomial time; different runtime guarantee

axisNote: The plot is a fixed-k density reference, not a claim that every variable-k threshold equals 1 or1/2. Exact n,k,ε conditions are beside the points. Green is sufficient density; red is conditional hardness below its boundary.
coverageNote: Bounded primary-source review completed 27 October 2026. Results are scoped comparisons, not an exhaustive or best-known-frontier claim.
lowerBoundStatus: Only the lower bounds explicitly shown apply to their labeled setup. An absent bound means no comparable bound was verified in this review.
